# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 24 (Bu-Vb Np24)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Np24
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 24
**Title (English, from literature):** Making a rainy-season robe at the wrong time
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin01m.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vassikasāṭika* ("Making a rainy-season robe at the wrong time") is the twenty-fourth rule in the *Nissaggiya Pācittiya* section of the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* in the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka. The text sets out the monastic regulation concerning the proper season for seeking and wearing rainy-season cloth: a monk who seeks or uses a rainy-season robe inappropriately commits an offense that requires relinquishment of the robe and formal confession. Modern translations include an English rendering by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 In Pali, it corresponds to the *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* rule (*pli-tv-bu-pm-np24*) and the *Bhikkhu Parivāra* (*Bhikkhu Parivāra Nissaggiya Pācittiya 24*). Parallels in other recensions include Sarvāstivāda vinaya texts (Chinese Vibhaṅga and Pātimokkha NP 28, Sanskrit Pātimokkha NP 26), Mūlasarvāstivāda versions preserved in Chinese, Tibetan, and Sanskrit (NP 28), Dharmaguptaka versions (Chinese NP 27), Mahīśāsaka versions (Chinese NP 17), Mahāsāṃghika and Lokottaravāda versions (Sanskrit and Chinese NP 25), as well as Kāśyapīya and Upāliparipṛcchā texts.

Text-reuse analysis in DharmaNexus identifies 530 matching passages across 78 Pali works [DharmaNexus]. The highest concentration of shared text occurs in formulaic legal definitions and procedural phrases shared with the *Bhikkhupātimokkha* and its sub-commentarial literature (*Vinayapiṭake Bhikkhupātimokkhapāḷi*, *Kaṅkhāvitaraṇīpurāṇa-ṭīkā*), the *Parivāra* (*Pvr 1.1*), the *Vattakkhandhaka* (*Kd 18*), and closely related *Nissaggiya Pācittiya* rules (notably Np 1, Np 7, Np 10, Np 12, Np 13, Np 16, Np 26, and Np 29) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments by DharmaNexus align passages with Tibetan Vinaya literature, specifically the *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003-4) and the *Prātimokṣasūtraṭīkā Vinayasamuccaya* (D4106-2), matching the Mūlasarvāstivāda lineage identified in curated parallel lists [DharmaNexus].
